_comment: TSBS cpu-only (DevOps) query set with FIXED parameters, shared by every engine of bench/telemetry.
Query shapes follow TSBS (github.com/timescale/tsbs, cmd/tsbs_generate_queries/uses/devops and
databases/{timescaledb,influx,questdb}/devops.go at the pinned commit); TSBS draws hosts and windows at
random per query instance, here one instance per type is written down so every engine answers the very
same question and the answers can be diffed.
Parameters were drawn once with Python random.Random(20160101): hosts from host_0..host_99 (valid for
any --scale >= 100), window starts uniformly in [2016-01-01, 2016-01-04 - window) at whole seconds, as
TSBS does (its windows are not aligned to bucket boundaries, so first and last buckets are partial).
The dataset must cover 2016-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2016-01-04T00:00:00Z (run.py checks it).
Placeholders in the dialect files: {HOSTS} = the host list as SQL string literals, {START}/{END} =
window bounds rendered per dialect (bench/compare/harness/queries.py render_time). Windows are
[START, END). Buckets are left-closed and aligned to the Unix epoch (date_bin / time_bucket / date_trunc /
SAMPLE BY ALIGN TO CALENDAR agree for 1 minute and 1 hour).
compare: keys identify a row; exact = equal values (max/min of float64 values are exact copies of stored
values); approx = relative tolerance (averages: summation order differs between engines).
timing: whether run.py times the query. transfer_heavy: the result has many rows, so client transfer
and decoding are a large part of the time (as in TSBS itself); reported, and flagged in the table.
